translation.text: When human beings multiplied in those days, beautiful and lovely daughters were born to them.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected expression is literally “children of men,” an ordinary designation of human beings. “Beautiful and lovely” retains both adjectives; no extra physical description has been added. The actual selected temporal form is እምዝ, not the old transcription እምዘ.

translation.text: The angels, the sons of heaven,[a] saw them and desired them. They said to one another, “Come, let us choose wives for ourselves from among human beings and father children for ourselves.”

footnotes.text: The selected text calls them “angels, sons of heaven.” This is retained without substituting a different classification. The invitation concerns choosing wives and begetting children; “desired” expresses the verb directly, without adding an unprinted description of their conduct.

translation.text: Simyaza, who was their leader,[a] said to them, “I fear that you may not be willing for this deed to be done, and that I alone will have to pay for this great sin.”

footnotes.text: The selected word for their leader belongs to a word family that also denotes an envoy or messenger; Dillmann1865 column49 attests its princely or leadership use. The verb at the close concerns paying or bearing the penalty for a sin, not enjoying a reward (columns1378–1379). “Simyaza” follows this verse’s spelling and is not silently conformed to the different printed name-form in 6:7.

translation.text: All of them answered him, “Let us all swear an oath and bind one another under a curse, so that we will not turn away from this plan but carry out this [plan] deed.”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected print has a star before the final “this” and brackets the repeated noun “plan”; its apparatus36 calls that noun an intrusion from the preceding clause. The deliberately awkward “[plan] deed” retains that printed bracketed word rather than silently deleting it or mistaking it for a reader-note anchor. The actual negative verb is ኢንመጠ, not the old transcription ኢንምጠ; Dillmann1865 columns214–215 support turning aside or withdrawing. Oath and mutual imprecation are distinct (columns155–156 and939–940). This is a translation of the selected critical text, not a claim that its bracketed repetition is secure ancient wording.

translation.text: Then they all swore together and bound one another under a curse by it.[a]

footnotes.text: The final ቦቱ is literally “in it” or “by it,” referring here to the oath just mentioned. No new geographical location is supplied. The oath and the mutual curse remain distinct actions; the latter is not silently reduced to a neutral agreement.

translation.text: They were all two hundred. †They descended into Ardis, which is the summit of Mount Hermon.† They called it Mount Hermon, because they swore there and bound one another under a curse.[a]

footnotes.text: This is a held literal draft, not an approved repair. Charles marks the entire descent/location clause with daggers. The selected words say “into Ardis” and describe a summit of Mount Hermon; a possible Jared-based repair discussed in the apparatus has not been adopted, nor has a generation of Jared been inserted from another translation. The selected stars before “two” and before the later mountain noun are retained in the source. The corruption affects a central location or chronological claim and still requires a separately sourced critical decision.

translation.text: These are the names of their angels: Śamīʾazāz—he was their leader—Arākiba⟦?⟧mēʾēl, Kokabiʾel, Ṭamiʾel, Ramiʾel, Danʾel, ʾEzēqēʾel, Beraqiyel, ʾAsaʾel, ʾArmaros, Beṭarʾel, ʾAnanʾel, Zaqēʾel, Samsapēʾel, Saterʾel, Ṭurʾel, Yomyaʾel, and †ʾArazyal†.[a]

footnotes.text: This is a held name-list draft. The first listed name after the leader has an unresolved medial vowel in the actual selected photograph; ⟦?⟧ records that uncertainty rather than substituting a familiar angel roster. The main text has a star before that first listed name and daggers around the final name. The superscript5 after ለ is an apparatus pointer, NOT an asterisk before “their angels”; the old false star has been removed. Printed unit7 continues through the coda now addressed as POB6:8. These transliterations do not certify historical name identities or normalize the list from another witness.
